newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer on Monday with dealers predicting they would fall during the week on the back of maturing treasury bills.
"The market is rather quiet at the moment but people are looking for 91-day treasury bills because they are anticipating a drop in the rates later and want to capitalise on that," a dealer said.
The dealers also said the central Reserve Bank had been in the market offering Z$1 billion worth of treasury bills.
"We expect the bills to be taken up because we have Z$825 million maturing today and some banks left some money in their accounts on Saturday," said one dealer.

Meanwhile on Monday morning, discount houses were selling treasury bills unchanged at 17.55 percent while bankers acceptance bills were indicated firmer at 18.15 (buying) from 17.75 percent but were selling at a steady 17.55 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought at 19 percent from 18.40 percent and sold at 18.25 percent, up from 18.15 percent and call money was quoted at 17.75 percent from 17 percent.
The market started with a surplus of Z$137 million.
